class="max-w-none markdown"><p>We are open sourcing our latest model, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi K2.6</strong>, featuring <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">state-of-the-art coding, long-horizon execution, and agent swarm capabilities</strong>. Kimi K2.6 is now available via <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi.com</a>, the Kimi App, the <a href="https://platform.kimi.com/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">API</a>, and <a href="/code/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi Code</a></strong>.</p>
<!--$?--><template id="B:0"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<!--$?--><template id="B:1"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<h2 node="[object Object]" id="long-horizon-coding">Long-Horizon Coding</h2>
<p>Kimi K2.6 shows strong improvements in long-horizon coding tasks, with reliable generalization across programming languages (e.g., Rust, Go, and Python) and tasks (e.g., front-end, devops, and performance optimization). On <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi Code Bench</strong>, our internal coding benchmark covering diverse complicated end-to-end tasks, Kimi K2.6 demonstrates significant improvements over Kimi K2.5.</p>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j305qav1fc641b5670?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Kimi Code Bench" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j305qav1fc641b5670?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j305qav1fc641b5670?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j305qav1fc641b5670?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j305qav1fc641b5670?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p>Kimi K2.6 demonstrates strong long-horizon coding in complex engineering tasks:</p>
<p>Kimi K2.6 successfully downloaded and deployed the <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Qwen3.5-0.8B</strong> model locally on a Mac. By implementing and optimizing model inference in <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Zig</strong>—a highly niche programming language—it demonstrated exceptional out-of-distribution generalization. Across <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">4,000+ tool calls, over 12 hours of continuous execution, and 14 iterations</strong>, Kimi K2.6 dramatically improved throughput from ~15 to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">~193 tokens/sec</strong>, ultimately achieving speeds ~20% faster than LM Studio.</p>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j1727f2ena623likig?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="K2.6 Qwen3.5-0.8B Mac inference optimization case" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j1727f2ena623likig?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j1727f2ena623likig?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j1727f2ena623likig?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j1727f2ena623likig?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p>Kimi K2.6 autonomously overhauled <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">exchange-core</strong>, an 8-year-old open-source financial matching engine. Over a <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">13-hour execution</strong>, the model iterated through 12 optimization strategies, initiating over 1,000 tool calls to precisely modify more than 4,000 lines of code. Acting as an expert systems architect, Kimi K2.6 analyzed CPU and allocation flame graphs to pinpoint hidden bottlenecks and boldly reconfigured the core thread topology (from 4ME+2RE to 2ME+1RE). Despite the engine already operating near its performance limits, Kimi K2.6 extracted a <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">185% medium throughput leap</strong> (from 0.43 to 1.24 MT/s) and a <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">133% performance throughput gain</strong> (soaring from 1.23 to 2.86 MT/s).</p>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j16siav1fc641arbr0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="K2.6 exchange-core coding showcase" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j16siav1fc641arbr0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j16siav1fc641arbr0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j16siav1fc641arbr0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j16siav1fc641arbr0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p>In beta tests, K2.6 performs well on long-horizon coding tasks in enterprise evaluations (randomly ordered):</p>

<h2 node="[object Object]" id="coding-driven-design">Coding-Driven Design</h2>
<p>Based on the strong coding capabilities, Kimi K2.6 can turn simple prompts into complete front-end interfaces, generating structured layouts with deliberate design choices such as aesthetic hero sections, as well as interactive elements and rich animations, including scroll-triggered effects. With strong proficiency in leveraging image and video generation tools, Kimi K2.6 supports the generation of visually coherent assets and contributes to higher-quality, more salient hero sections.</p>
<p>Moreover, Kimi K2.6 expands beyond static frontend development to simple full-stack workflows—spanning authentication to user interaction to database operations for lightweight use cases like transaction logging or session management.</p>
<p>We established an internal <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi Design Bench</strong>, organized into four categories: Visual Input Tasks, Landing Page Construction, Full-Stack Application Development, and General Creative Programming. In comparison with Google AI Studio, Kimi K2.6 shows promising results and performs well across these categories.</p>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j30aiav1fc641b5710?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Kimi Design Bench" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j30aiav1fc641b5710?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j30aiav1fc641b5710?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j30aiav1fc641b5710?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j30aiav1fc641b5710?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p>Below are examples generated by <a href="/en/build" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.6 Agent</a> from a single prompt, with preconfigured harnesses and tools:</p>

<h2 node="[object Object]" id="agent-swarms-elevated">Agent Swarms, Elevated</h2>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Scaling out, not just up.</strong> An Agent Swarm dynamically decomposes tasks into heterogeneous subtasks executed concurrently by self-created domain-specialized agents.</p>
<p>Based on the K2.5 Agent Swarm research preview, <a href="/en/agent-swarm" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi K2.6 Agent Swarm</a> demonstrates <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">a qualitative leap</strong> in the agent swarm experience. It seamlessly coordinates heterogeneous agents to combine complementary skills: broad search layered with deep research, large-scale document analysis fused with long-form writing, and multi-format content generation executed in parallel. This compositional intelligence enables the swarm to deliver end-to-end outputs—spanning documents, websites, slides, and spreadsheets—within a single autonomous run.</p>
<p>The architecture scales horizontally to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">300 sub-agents executing across 4,000 coordinated steps simultaneously</strong>, a substantial expansion from K2.5&#x27;s 100 sub-agents and 1,500 steps. This massive parallelization fundamentally reduces end-to-end latency while significantly enhancing output quality and expanding the operational boundaries of Agents swarms.</p>
<p>It can also turn any high-quality files such as PDFs, spreadsheets, slides, and Word documents into <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Skills</strong>. Kimi K2.6 captures and maintains the documents&#x27; structural and stylistic DNA, enabling you to reproduce the same quality and format in future tasks.</p>
<p>Here are some examples:</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<h2 node="[object Object]" id="proactive-agents">Proactive Agents</h2>
<p>K2.6 demonstrates strong performance in autonomous, proactive agents such as <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="https://openclaw.ai/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">OpenClaw</a></strong> and <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hermes</a></strong>, which operate across multiple applications with continuous, 24/7 execution.</p>
<p>Unlike simple chat-based interactions, these workflows require AI to proactively manage schedules, execute code, and orchestrate cross-platform operations as a persistent background agent.</p>
<p>Our RL infra team used a K2.6-backed agent that operated autonomously for <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">5 days</strong>, managing monitoring, incident response, and system operations, demonstrating persistent context, multi-threaded task handling, and full-cycle execution from alert to resolution. Here is K2.6&#x27;s worklog (anonymized to remove sensitive information):</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<p>Kimi K2.6 delivers measurable improvements in real-world reliability: more precise API interpretation, stabler long-running performance, and enhanced safety awareness during extended research tasks.</p>
<p>Performance gains are quantified by our internal <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Claw Bench</strong>, the evaluation suite spanning five domains: Coding Tasks, IM Ecosystem Integration, Information Research &amp; Analysis, Scheduled Task Management, and Memory Utilization. Across all metrics, Kimi K2.6 significantly outperforms Kimi K2.5 in task completion rates and tool invocation accuracy—particularly in workflows requiring sustained autonomous operation without human oversight.</p>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j2vv53v89kkei5on5g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Kimi Claw Bench" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j2vv53v89kkei5on5g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j2vv53v89kkei5on5g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j2vv53v89kkei5on5g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-04-20/1d7j2vv53v89kkei5on5g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<h2 node="[object Object]" id="bring-your-own-agents">Bring Your Own Agents</h2>
<p>Building upon Kimi K2.6&#x27;s robust orchestration capabilities, Kimi K2.6 extends your proactive agents to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Claw Groups</strong> as a research preview—a new instantiation of the Agent Swarm architecture.</p>
<p>Claw Groups embrace an open, heterogeneous ecosystem: Multiple agents and humans operate as true collaborators. Users can onboard agents from any device, running any model, each carrying their own specialized toolkits, skills and persistent memory contexts. Whether deployed on local laptops, mobile devices, or cloud instances, these diverse agents integrate seamlessly into a shared operational space.</p>
<p>At the center of this swarm, Kimi K2.6 serves as an adaptive coordinator. It dynamically matches tasks to agents based on their specific skill profiles and available tools, optimizing for capability fit. When an agent encounters failure or stalls, the coordinator detects the interruption, automatically reassigns the task or regenerates subtasks, and actively manages the full lifecycle of deliverables—from initiation through validation to completion.</p>
<p>We also want to thank the K2.6-powered agents in Claw Groups—we&#x27;ve been dogfooding our own agent marketing team by refining human–agent workflows in practice. Using Claw Groups, we run end-to-end content production and launch campaigns, with specialized agents like Demo Makers, Benchmark Makers, Social Media Agents, and Video Makers working together. K2.6 coordinates the process, enabling agents to share intermediate results and turn ideas into consistent, fully packaged deliverables.</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<p>We are moving beyond simply asking AI a question or assigning AI a task, and entering a phase where human and AI collaborate as genuine partners—combining strengths to solve problems collectively. Claw Groups marks our latest efforts toward a future where the boundaries between &quot;my agent,&quot; &quot;your agent,&quot; and &quot;our team&quot; dissolve seamlessly into a collaborative system.</p>
<h2 node="[object Object]" id="benchmark-table">Benchmark Table</h2>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:360px"></div></div>
<p>To reproduce official Kimi-K2.6 benchmark results, we recommend using the official API. For third-party providers, refer to Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV) to choose high-accuracy services. Details: <a href="/en/blog/kimi-vendor-verifier" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-vendor-verifier</a></p>
<h2 node="[object Object]" id="footnotes">Footnotes</h2>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">1. General Testing Details</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>We report results for Kimi K2.6 and Kimi K2.5 with thinking mode enabled, Claude Opus 4.6 with max effort, GPT-5.4 with xhigh reasoning effort, and Gemini 3.1 Pro with a high thinking level.</li>
<li>Unless otherwise specified, all Kimi K2.6 experiments were conducted with temperature = 1.0, top-p = 1.0, and a context length of 262,144 tokens.</li>
<li>Benchmarks without publicly available scores were re-evaluated under the same conditions used for Kimi K2.6 and are marked with an asterisk (*). Except where noted with an asterisk, all other results are cited from official reports.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">2. Reasoning Benchmarks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>IMO-AnswerBench scores for GPT-5.4 and Claude 4.6 were obtained from <a href="https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.1" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.1</a>.</li>
<li>Humanity&#x27;s Last Exam (HLE) and other reasoning tasks were evaluated with a maximum generation length of 98,304 tokens. By default, we report results on the HLE full set. For the text-only subset, Kimi K2.6 achieves 36.4% accuracy without tools and 55.5% with tools.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">3. Tool-Augmented / Agentic Tasks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Kimi K2.6 was equipped with search, code-interpreter, and web-browsing tools for HLE with tools, BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and WideSearch.</li>
<li>For HLE-Full with tools, the maximum generation length is 262,144 tokens with a per-step limit of 49,152 tokens. We employ a simple context management strategy: once the context window exceeds the threshold, only the most recent round of tool-related messages is retained.</li>
<li>For BrowseComp, we report scores obtained with context management using the same discard-all strategy as Kimi K2.5 and DeepSeek-V3.2.</li>
<li>For DeepSearchQA, no context management was applied to Kimi K2.6 tests, and tasks exceeding the supported context length were directly counted as failed. Scores for Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro on DeepSearchQA are cited from the <a href="https://cdn.sanity.io/files/4zrzovbb/website/037f06850df7fbe871e206dad004c3db5fd50340.pdf" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Claude Opus 4.7 System Card</a>.</li>
<li>For WideSearch, we report results under the &quot;hide tool result&quot; context management setting. Once the context window exceeds the threshold, only the most recent round of tool-related messages is retained.</li>
<li>The test system prompts are identical to those used in the <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.02276" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Kimi K2.5 technical report</a>.</li>
<li>Claw Eval was conducted using version 1.1 with max-tokens-per-step = 16384.</li>
<li>For APEX-Agents, we evaluate 452 tasks from the public 480-task release, as done by <a href="https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/apex-agents-aa" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Artificial Analysis</a> (excluding Investment Banking Worlds 244 and 246, which have external runtime dependencies).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">4. Coding Tasks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Terminal-Bench 2.0 scores were obtained with the default agent framework (Terminus-2) and the provided JSON parser, operating in preserve thinking mode.</li>
<li>For the SWE-Bench series of evaluations (including Verified, Multilingual, and Pro), we used an in-house evaluation framework adapted from SWE-agent. This framework includes a minimal set of tools—bash tool, createfile tool, insert tool, view tool, strreplace tool, and submit tool.</li>
<li>All reported scores for coding tasks are averaged over 10 independent runs.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">5. Vision Benchmarks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Max-tokens = 98,304, averaged over three runs (avg@3).</li>
<li>Settings with Python tool use max-tokens-per-step = 65,536 and max-steps = 50 for multi-step reasoning.</li>
<li>MMMU-Pro follows the official protocol, preserving input order and prepending images.</li>
</ul></div></section></div></div><nav class="BlogV2MiniNav-module__1w6TBa__miniNav blog-v2-mini-nav" aria-label="Article sections" data-variant="default"><div
